M O R E   M A I L ! !


    October, 1992    Page Reply

 How to write to us...02     -
 A.C. Moir............03    04
 L.G. Baumann.........06    12
 Garry Rowland........13     -
 Malcolm Perry........16    20
 Miles Kinloch........21    26
 Ted Felstead.........29    32
 Ray Barnes...........34    38
 John McCabe..........40    43

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From: A. C. Moir,
      P.O. Box 26,
      BOGNOR REGIS,
      West Sussex  PO22 0JQ

Dear Ron,

I am running a 128K Spectrum
with +D disc drive. Is there, to
your knowledge, or perhaps your
readers knowledge, any way of
retrieving data from drive back
to cassette?

Also, are there any other +D
users interested in correspond-
ence regarding +D, or perhaps a
+D user group?

        Yours sincerely,

            Andy Moir

Brian Cavers to A.C. Moir

I do not know of any software to
transfer files from +D to tape.I
desperately need such a program
myself since I must monthly move
OUTLET from +D to tape,Opus, +3,
and microdrive all via tape and
it all has to be done manually!

I assume from your question that
you mean an automatic, mass copy
of disc software to tape because
it is not too difficult to copy
individual files - it is merely
time-consuming. You simply read
the CAT details, load and save
to tape accordingly. Of course,
some BASIC syntax may need
changing if it is to run from
tape.


May I ask why you want to move
software from disc to tape? If,
for example, you only want to
transfer code files, say text
files, I could write a simple
program to copy most such files
I think.

As for direct correspondence to
other +D users, as stated at the
start of these pages every month
anyone can ask for his full
address to be published and ask
for direct contact and OUTLET
itself acts as a user group.What
more could you ask of a user
group that you don't get from
OUTLET? You get regular info,
letters from others, help and
advice, programs and articles as
well as direct contacts if you
want them.             - Brian

From: L.G. Baumann, SOUTH AFRICA

Reverting again to Malcolm
Goodman's puzzle -

      "so that you can  find
    out what value you  gave
    to (say) K or N$"

I, unfortunately, did not
realise that a string of letters
is, in computer jargon, also
considered to be a "value" -
hence my solution last month
based solely on numeric values.
So to make good I am enclosing
three variations on a theme all
of which will work. In each case
the string v$ is added to the
end of string w$ and later the
strings are re-constituted.

For simplicity I have not
incuded any error traps in the
listing.
          Variation 1
          -----------
In this listing 26 PRINT lines
are used and the computer is
directed to the appropriate
print line (100 onwards) by line
32

[SAM owners should substitute an
alternative variable name to
LENGTH,say LNGTH, because LENGTH
is a SAM keyword and will not be
accepted as a variable name.-BC]

 20 LET length = LEN w$
 21 LET w$=w$+v$
 30 INPUT "variable? ";v$
 31 IF LEN v$=1 THEN  PRINT  VAL

 V$: GO TO 50
 32 If LEN v$=2 THEN GO TO  CODE
 v$(1)+3
 50 LET v$=w$(length+1 TO )
 51 LET W$=w$( TO length)
 60 STOP
100 PRINT a$: GO TO 50
101 PRINT b$: GO TO 50
102 PRINT c$: GO TO 50

    ETC  ........

120 PRINT u$: GO TO 50
121 PRINT w$(length TO ): GO  TO
 50 REM for v$
122 PRINT w$( TO length): Go  TO
 50 REM for w$
123 PRINT x$: GO TO 50
124 PRINT y$: GO TO 50
125 PRINT z$: GO TO 50


          Variation 2
          ------------

In this case a single long LINE
carries all the string PRINT
references i.e. LINE 100. The
computer is directed by LINE 32
to this LINE and to the right
Statement in that Line by poking
the System Variables Addresses.


 20 LET length  =  LEN  w$:  LET
    bb=50

 21 LET w$=w$+v$

 30 INPUT "variable? ";v$

 31 IF LEN v$=1 THEN  PRINT  VAL
    V$: GO TO 50


 32 If LEN v$=2 THEN POKE 23662,
  100: POKE 23663,0: POKE 23664,
  (CODE V$(1)-96)*2: CONTINUE

 50 LET v$=w$(length+1 TO )

 51 LET W$=w$( TO length)

100  STOP   :  PRINT  a$: GO  TO
 bb: PRINT b$ : GO TO bb:  PRINT
 c$: GO TO bb...................
 PRINT w$( length+1  TO ): GO TO
 bb: PRINT w$( TO length): GO TO
 bb: PRINT x$: GO TO bb: etc.

          Variation 3
          -----------

Probably the neatest. This uses
the idea you put forward - to
poke an address to change the
String letter.

Line 1 is used for this and LINE
32 makes the change in it. The
program should be started with
GO TO 20.

  1 PRINT a$: STOP
 20 LET length = LEN w$
 21 LET w$=w$+v$
 22 LET flag=2
 30 INPUT "variable? ";v$
 31 IF LEN v$=1 THEN  PRINT  VAL
    V$: LET flag =1 : GO TO 50
 32 If LEN v$=2 THEN POKE  (PEEK
    23635+256*PEEK  23636+5),
    CODE v$(1)
 50 LET v$=w$(length+1 TO )
 51 LET W$=w$( TO length)
 52 IF flag=2 THEN GO TO 1
 53 STOP
               Regards,

             L.G.Baumann

Brian Cavers to L.G. Baumann

That solution variation 1 might
also be improved by using say,
PRINT VAL$ V$ (except for V$ and
W$) instead of all the PRINT a$,
PRINT b$, etc. with a slight
adjustment of other lines.

In addition I think line 121
should be w$(length+1 TO) not
w$(length TO) as shown.

Great anyway!

                        - Brian

From: Garry Rowland, DAGENHAM


Dear Brian,

No sooner had I posted my letter
(the one that appeared in "more
letters" OUTLET 61) than...
excuse me, I just have to wipe
some egg off my face... I find
half a dozen enquiries in my
mail mentioning a review in
Sinclair User!

Waiting for a quiet moment in
WHS, I furtively flicked through
SU. I'm just over forty and it's
becoming an embarrassment to
have to pick out the "Speccy-
weccy comics" from the piles of
PC, Amiga and Atari magazines.

However, embarrassment overcome,
I found the mention of PFN print
system in SU. As usual they were
way over the top. I'm sure their
hearts are in the right place
though, so all is forgiven. My
apologies for any slurs made
upon the characters of those at
SU (and YS too, just in case).

Tabloid. I just thought I'd
mention that word again.

Your mention about markets and
timing is very true. However, my
aim wasn't to make a fortune -
after a long term of unemploy-
ment, it was simply a case of
trying to survive doing some-
thing I enjoyed.I was aware that
Music Writer had arrived late, I
just hadn't realised how late.

But I'm in some "high flying"
company. I see that Ratners are
closing 110 shops and moving up-
market! They have the capital to
do it - I don't, which is why
I'm now turning to writing prog-
rams for the public domain as a
form of self expression. Some-
thing OUTLET has been encourag-
ing all its members for some
time. Lets hope it can continue
to do so for some time yet.

        Yours sincerely,

         Garry Rowland

From: Malc Perry, KIDDERMINSTER

Dear Brian and Ron,

I have had a spell with the
Disciple writing on sectors in
current use and when it wrote
program data into the directory
area it was obvious there was a
problem. This turned out to be
due to a faulty ribbon cable
connection and the side select
signal was not reliably getting
to the drive. The Disciple was
saying "use side two" but the
drive was staying on side 1.

This is how the Discsearch
program came to be written to
find out what was going on and
recover text files. (OUTLET
Issue 51).

I believe some odd corruptions
are due to dirty edge connectors
that upset the sector map data
in memory. After a few corrupt-
ions over a few days the system
failed completly due to the edge
connector; cleaning resolved
both problems.

When I first had the Disciple I
had a lot of problems due to
badly corrupted files which in
this case was my own doing. The
Save would stop with 'overwrite
...?' message and I would think
"wrong disc", change disc and
continue by hitting the "Y" key.
of course, the DOS was still
using the data held for the old
disc so would write to sectors
that were free on the previous
disc but not on the second one.

There are problems when using
"opentype" files but this is
mainly that the +D gets confused
when using 2 drives and over
which is which.

I have never, as far as I am
aware, had a problem on a Save
following "write protected" or
"disc full" related messages,
either on the +D or on the
Disciple. (i.e. using +D with
48k and Disciples with 48k and
128k). Perhaps there is a
problem with other machines such
as +2a or +3 that I would be
unaware of as I am not using
either of them.

There is a bug in the Disciple
in that the DOS does not reset
after a "full disc" message and

so will not Save to any other
disc. There was a poke to cure
this in Format but it never
worked for me.

I find the easiest way to test
for a corruption on Saves is to
set up an 'Auto Save' routine
that simply prints a number to
the screen then Saves the screen
with the number as the file
name, then increment the number
by 1 and so on until the disc is
full. A simple 'Auto Load'
routine then displays the
screens in turn and it's obvious
if something has been corrupted.

         Malcolm Perry

Brian Cavers to Malcolm Perry

I have been suffering corrupt +D
discs too which seems to be the
directory bit map going wrong
somehow. I have not tracked down
what is causing it yet though. I
may have another go at cleaning
the edge connector.

I also found the POKE to correct
the Disciple full disc message
bug didn't work. It must be
solveable though because it must
be due to some flag in memory
not being reset. Perhaps the way
to find it is have a full disc
ready, save low RAM to another
disc; try to save low RAM to the
full disc; load the previous RAM
to high memory; then compare the
two!                   - Brian

From: Miles Kinloch, EDINBURGH

Dear Brian,

You'll be pleased to know I've
finally taken the plunge and
ordered a +D and two drives from
Datel. When they arrive, I'll
probably be very busy setting
everything up and experimenting
etc., so thought I'd write now
while I have a spare moment.

By coincidence my OUTLET subs-
cription is also due for renewal
but I'm faced with a dilemma and
wondered if you could advise. If
I switched over to the +D OUTLET
now,would this mean I would have
to miss out on the rest of the
ROM Index files which have still
to appear on tape?

If so, for the sake of having
the set complete, I would prefer
just to continue with the tape
version until they are finished,
though I would like to start
getting the disk OUTLET as soon
as possible. By the way,does the
+D version have any +D exclusive
items that don't appear on tape?

Regarding the 'variable not
found' error in MENUMASTER which
Chris Clayton mentioned last
month, I have to report that I
too experienced exactly the same
thing when I tried to run that
program.The variable in question
is the array variable t$ in line
360, and the error seems to come
about because there is no DIM
command in line 8805 before the
array is loaded.

I was wondering if maybe in the
version you tested and found to
be O.K. perhaps t$ had already
been DIMmed as a direct command
and saved with the program, thus
enabling the array to be loaded
in successfully? (By the way,
what should the DIMensions be?)

Finally,a word or two about that
intriguing problem regarding
printing variables. You know, it
strikes me, Brian, that your
SCREEN$ method might work after
all with just a small modificat-
ion. Up to line 50 your original
routine works fine...

10 DECLARE VARIABLES ETC...
20 CLS: PRINT "VARIABLE? "
30 PAUSE 0: PRINT INKEY$;

40 PAUSE 0: PRINT INKEY$
50 IF SCREEN$ (1,1)=" " THEN
PRINT VAL SCREEN$ (1,0): STOP

The only problem thereafter was
caused by the SCREEN$ bug,
caused by adding two SCREEN$
characters together. If you now
have as line 60, however...

60 PRINT VAL$ (SCREEN$
(1,0)+"$")

...that appears to do the trick,
since the second character, "$",
is pre-determined and does not
need to be read from the screen.

Finally, let me say how sorry I
was to hear about the financial
difficulties you're facing with
OUTLET just now. I do hope they

are only temporary, as OUTLET is
in a class of its own and its
demise would be a bitter blow
for the serious Spectrum user. I
personally would not object to a
price increase, as even at twice
the price it would still repre-
sent good value for money. When
one considers that some commer-
cial software houses charge as
much for a single program as you
do for a whole Issue of OUTLET,
it really does put things into
perspective!

            Regards,

         Miles Kinloch

Brian Cavers to Miles Kinloch

There are only about 3 months of
ROM INDEX left on the tape but I
shall put these with your next
+D issue to save messing. No,the
+D version has never had any +D
exclusive items that are not on
the tape version too although it
is remotely possible a future
issue might have an odd item for
some special reason. Often items
will run immediately on another
system but the OUTLET links will
not work and other syntax might
need altering sometimes.

I now see the MENUMASTER error
is on the tape version only. I
had only re-checked the +D! This
is what you do...

Change line 8805 to line 8815
and delete line 8805. It is a
CLEAR statement in line 8810
that is wiping out t$() as soon
as it was loaded at line 8805!
If t$() is loaded at 8810 it
works but messes up the title
page with the load prompt (the
reason why I moved it on the
tape version at the last minute)
A neater solution would be to
move the CLEAR statement from
line 8810 to the start of line
8805 (but replace the CLEAR in
line 8810 with a CLS). Alternat-
ively, return your tape for a
replacement. Sorry about the
hassle.

Incidentally, you do not need to
DIMension any array before load-
ing it.

I rather like your solution to
the puzzle, especially the...

 PRINT VAL$(SCREEN$(1,0)+"$") !

Your method is one of the most
compact I think. It would be a
"true" use of VAL$ except the
puzzle is academic (because one
need only enter PRINT A$ etc.).
I have yet to see a genuine use
of VAL$ in a real program. I
suspect it may only ever be of
use in a routine used by a BASIC
programmer. I have only twice in
9 years found what I thought was
a use in one of my own programs
only to reject it because there
was a better method and I would
have been using VAL$ just for
the sake of it! Has anyone else
a GENUINE use of VAL$? - Brian

From: Ted Felstead,
"Iona" Billinge Road, Highfield,
 WIGAN  WN3 6BL

In response to your request for
ways to maintain OUTLET, I would
like to say that I would be
willing to pay an increased
subscription to enable such an
excellent magazine to continue.

I would also be very willing to
help in any way I could and
would certainly be willing to
contribute any material to the
magazine totally free to you.

To this end I have tackled the
problem of the 26 variables as
outlined in the last Issue. I am
not certain that I totally
understood the problem but on

the enclosed disc [in ADDENDERS]
is a program which allows the
declaration of 26 numeric and 26
string variables and also random
access to them. I hope it may be
of some interest.

I was very sad to read about the
problems of Samco, particularly
as I was intending to upgrade to
a SAM as soon as funds allowed.
It would be a shame if such a
project were to die completely,
especially since it encompassed
Spectrum BASIC which must be one
of the most user-friendly BASICs
around.

I had a demonstration of SAM
from Derek Morgan (who writes to
you regularly) and I was very
impressed with the machine.

I assume you will be keeping us
up to date about developments
regarding SAM and its future, or
not, as the case may be. I would
like you to publish my full name
and address as I would welcome
any direct correspondance from
your readers. Best wishes for
the future which I hope will
mean we receive OUTLET for many
more years.

        Yours sincerely,

         Ted Felstead.

Brian Cavers to Ted Felstead

I'll put your program in ADD-
ENDERS with the name "TWENTY6"
if I can because it is a bit
long to list here.It's main idea
is to accept a single keypress
using INKEY$ where a lower case
letter is taken as a string
variable: a$ to z$ and a shifted
keypress as a numeric variable:
A to Z. There is then a list...

IF INKEY$="a" THEN PRINT a$
IF INKEY$="b" THEN PRINT b$
IF INKEY$="A" THEN PRINT A
                   ...and so on.
This is fine although INKEY$ is
often missed in such a long list
if the user releases the key so
CHR$ PEEK 23560 may be better.


This puzzle has attracted a lot
of different ideas and I've not
yet opened the solution sent in
by the original poser: Malcolm
Goodman (er... perhaps I should
rephrase that!). If anyone can
think up any more brain-teasers
then please send them!

News about SAM developments will
normally only appear in the SAM
issue, Ted, because generally
readers want separate magazines.
However, major news items like:
"GOVERNMENT TO INVEST 6 BILLION
IN SAM COUPE" would be reported
in the Spectrum version too.

                        - Brian

From: R. Barnes, WESTBURY

Business is slow again here in
the shop as you probably know if
you watch the telly so I thought
I'd have another ramble on at
you. I have waited for the last
two issues of OUTLET with bated
breath. After you gave those
instructions for loading
Minichrw in Tasword I waited for
the outcry that it didn't work,
at least I couldn't get it to
work properly. But the outcry
didn't come so I set out to
solve the problem myself by
'hooking' the font out of
Tasword +3, modifying it, and
putting it back, and for those
who couldn't get it to work
either here is the M O.


I used Tasword +3, Extendacat,
Chargen, Minichrw and a blank
disk. Chargen appears to be
faulty, it saves all fonts all
the time and its output needs
slicing up. I also learnt a bit
too; I didn't know you could
slice code up like this, but I
do now.
1) Load"Tastable.bin" Code53248,
   12288

2) Save "Mintext" Code53504,768
   (to blank disk )

3) Reset, load "CHARGEN"

4) Load "Mintext" into font 1

5) Modify font. (I loaded
   Minichrw into font 2 to use
   as a reference)

6) Save font as "FINAL"to blank.
  (This saves as "FINAL" Code
   60160,4608

7) Reset, reload "Final" Code
   60160,4608

8) Resave as "MINI"Code 60160,
   768

9) Load Tasword, into BASIC,
   load "MINI"Code 53504 and
   'Hey Presto'

10) Stop Tasword, save modified
    Tasword

Now then, a few months ago I
became the proud? owner of an
Atari 1040 STE. What a pain in
the backside it is. It's so slow
compared with the +3.

Its graphic possibilities are
good but they don't seem to be
used much in commercial programs
- even using the simplest
programs like a word proc makes
life a wriggling torment. You
will be pleased to hear that
except when the kids come and
want to play a 'Tank battle' or
I want to draw pretty pictures
it spends 90% of its time on top
of the wardrobe - which to me
seems the best place for it.
Seriously though the machine has
been 'hyped' out of all
proportion to its advantages.


What do you think of Tasword
with the new font?
                   - Ray Barnes

Brian Cavers to Ray Barnes



Yes, as reported last month,when
I came to try to put minichrW in
Tasword +3 I realized it was the
wrong sort of font and that it
had been adapted for WORDMASTER
type files originally. The other
MINICHAR files in last month's
issue work fine though.


I agree about the ST. I only use
mine to get PD screens for the
SAM these days.The wordprocessor
I used on it was pretty dreadful
although I'm sure there is much
better software - if you have
lots of cash to spare!

By the way, since you run a bike
shop, have you got those new
tubeless tyres yet that were
reported on Tomorrow's World on
television a few months ago?

They were a sort of solid
plastic full of bubbles that you
never needed to inflate and you
could run over a nail without
ever getting a puncture! I guess
they'd be expensive?

                        - Brian

From: J. McCabe, SURREY

I was intrigued by the puzzle
set in August's OUTLET and I
decided to tackle it. I used a
Spectrum for six years before
getting a SAM.

After a great deal of trial and
error, I eventually managed to
come up with a solution I hope
will work on both machiines. The
address used to store INKEY$ is
the svar SEED, which is common
to both computers. The listing
is included below.

I have greatly enjoyed the
challenge of solving this
problem and would look forward
to seeing more puzzles set.

How about making it a regular
feature?

 10 LET A=1, B=2, C=3, D=4

 20 LET A$"SAM",B$="SPECTRUM",
    C$="BASIC",D$="PUZZLE"

 30 REM   ETC...ETC.....

100 PRINT "VARIABLE?   ":
    PAUSE 0

110 PRINT INKEY$:

120 POKE 23670,CODE INKEY$
    PAUSSE 100

125 REM  TWO SECONDS ALLOWED TO
    PRESS "$"

130 PRINT INKEY$:" = ":

140 IF INKEY$="$" THEN PRINT
    (VAL$ (CHR$ PEEK 23670+"$"))

150 PRINT VAL CHR$ PEEK 23670
    GO TO 100

           Regards,

         John McCabe


Brian Cavers to John McCabe

Another good solution although I
would prefer a PAUSE 0 instead
of the PAUSE 100 at line 120 and
a prompt to "enter" the variable
(i.e. press ENTER afterwards).
If the PAUSE 0 at line 120 were
then followed by a test for the
ENTER key being pressed and a
further PAUSE 0 if it is not
(i.e. if instead "$" is pressed)
then the further PAUSE 0 would
accept the ENTER key.

I'd be quite happy for readers
to send in further puzzles. If I
think up any of my own I'll put
them in. I mentioned elsewhere
I would dearly love to see a
program that is genuinely using
VAL$!                   - Brian.

В этом листинге используются 26 строк PRINT, и компьютер направляется к соответствующей строке печати (начиная со 100) строкой 32.

*(Владельцам SAM следует заменить имя переменной LENGTH на другое, например LNGTH, поскольку LENGTH является ключевым словом в SAM и не будет принято в качестве имени переменной. — Б.К.)*

```text
 20 LET length = LEN w$
 21 LET w$=w$+v$
 30 INPUT "variable? ";v$
 31 IF LEN v$=1 THEN PRINT VAL v$: GO TO 50
 32 IF LEN v$=2 THEN GO TO CODE v$(1)+3
 50 LET v$=w$(length+1 TO )
 51 LET w$=w$( TO length)
 60 STOP
100 PRINT a$: GO TO 50
101 PRINT b$: GO TO 50
102 PRINT c$: GO TO 50

121 PRINT w$(length TO ): GO TO 50 REM для v$
122 PRINT w$( TO length): GO TO 50 REM для w$

125 PRINT z$: GO TO 50
```

#### Вариант 2

В этом случае одна длинная СТРОКА содержит все обращения PRINT к строкам, т.е. СТРОКА 100. Компьютер направляется СТРОКОЙ 32 к этой СТРОКЕ и к нужному оператору в ней с помощью poke в адреса системных переменных.

```text

 32 IF LEN v$=2 THEN POKE 23662,100: POKE 23663,0: POKE 23664,(CODE v$(1)-96)*2: CONTINUE
 50 LET v$=w$(length+1 TO )

100 STOP: PRINT a$: GO TO bb: PRINT b$: GO TO bb: PRINT c$: GO TO bb...................

```

Для этого используется строка 1, а СТРОКА 32 вносит в неё изменения. Программу следует запускать с GO TO 20.

```text

 21 LET w$=w$+v$
 22 LET flag=2

 53 STOP
```
